shoes.title: Taking Off Shoes in Japan: 5 Things to Know
shoes.desc: Visiting a Japanese home or ryokan? At many entrances (genkan) there is a small step, and you take your shoes off before it. Some restaurants, temples and fitting rooms may also ask you to remove shoes. Wear clean socks, take slippers off before stepping onto tatami, and leave toilet slippers in the toilet room. Customs vary, so follow signs and staff. Get the free 1-page Japan Quick Start cheat sheet. #japantravel #japantips #firsttimeinjapan

Note: customs vary, follow signs and staff. Save this for your trip! Footer: free 1-page cheat sheet, Japan Quick Start.

escalator.title: Escalators in Japan: 5 Things to Know
escalator.desc: Which side do you stand on? In the Tokyo area, people often stand on the left. In the Osaka area, people often stand on the right. Some stations and cities ask everyone to stand on both sides and not walk. Not sure? Stand where the people in front of you are standing, hold the handrail, and watch big suitcases. Rules vary by area and station. Get the free 1-page Japan Quick Start cheat sheet. #japantravel #japantips #firsttimeinjapan

lost.title: Lost Something in Japan? 5 Things to Do
lost.desc: Lost your wallet, phone or bag in Japan? Ask at a koban (a small police box); officers can help you report a lost item. Lost it on a train or in a station? Ask station staff or the lost & found. Write down when and where you lost it and which train or line you used. Keep taxi receipts; they often show the company name, and hotel staff can often help you make calls. Steps vary, so ask staff for help. Get the free 1-page Japan Quick Start cheat sheet. #japantravel #japantips #firsttimeinjapan
